messages:
Maya: Heads up — HF->Redwood conversion produced garbled special tokens in chat templates for the mpt-6b-charset import. Evals show a ~5% drop on dialog-turn F1 after conversion.
Jon: Can you paste the exact tokenization output you're seeing?
Maya: Quick snippet from the converter run: 
```
2026-02-05 10:12:34 converter INFO: loading tokenizer from hf://org/mpt-6b-charset
2026-02-05 10:12:34 converter WARN: special_tokens_map.json charset=windows-1252
2026-02-05 10:12:34 converter ERROR: mapped token '<|system|>' -> '\\x93system\\x94' (bytes) when serializing special tokens
```
Priyanka: That looks like the charset auto-detect fallback triggered. If special_tokens_map.json lacks a unicode BOM/marker our loader falls back to latin1/windows-1252 in one codepath and utf-8 in another, then we end up persisting inconsistent keys.
Jon: Oof — downstream, the safetensors shard index gets those garbled keys as weight-name metadata and our weight-key-rename pass doesn't match them, so state_dict load becomes inconsistent. Any example of the weight rename failure?
Maya: Yes — quant pipeline failing with: `KeyError: 'lm_head'` while the converter's state dict contains `\x93lm_head\x94` (garbled). Also saw `RuntimeError: safetensors shard index checksum mismatch` after a retry during hub download.
Jon: Two separate but interacting bugs: (1) charset fallback for special_tokens_map.json -> garbled special token keys; (2) hub download/revision pin race where a partial shard finishes then gets replaced by a different revision with same filename, converter concatenates entries and doesn't verify sha256 in index.json.
Priyanka: Repro steps I used: 
```
# repro
hf-sync pull org/mpt-6b-charset --revision main --out=tmp/
python -m redwood_convert --input tmp/ --output converted/ --pin-revision main
# then run our chat-template smoke eval
python eval/chat_smoke.py --model converted/ --template=chat_v1
```
Jon: Workaround if you need immediate unblock: set `CONVERTER_FORCE_UTF8=1` in env and re-run conversion, and use `--lock-revision` (converter will fail if remote revision metadata changes). That normalized the tokens for me and restored eval scores to baseline within ~0.8%.
Maya: I also reran the 8-bit quant experiment with the fixed mapping; quantized model matched baseline generation quality and latency was unchanged. We should canary this change since it's critical for chat templates.
devops-bot: canary deploy started for pipeline/converter v2026-02-05-rc3 
Priyanka: I'll open a PR: add explicit utf-8 enforcement when reading special_tokens_map.json, add a unit test that simulates CP1252-encoded special_tokens_map, and add sha256 verification against shard index.json during download. Also add a small eval in CI: run chat-template smoke and assert no tokenization surprises.
Maya: Thanks — dropping eval diffs and logs at /tmp/redwood-debug/1767777777/ (includes tokenization dumps, shard index.json, and quant logs).
Jon: I'll implement a regex-based fallback for weight-key renames (handles common dot-order permutations) and make the rename log a WARN that includes both original and mapped names so we can spot garbled ones earlier. Also adding a fail-fast when a key mismatch looks like non-utf8.
hf-sync-bot: Hub sync alert: 1 file MD5 mismatch for org/mpt-6b-charset @2026-02-05T10:13:01Z
Maya: tagging @Priyanka and @Jon for follow-ups. I'll hold the canary evaluation until PR lands. :thumbsup:
Jon: On it. Plan: patch, unit tests + replay on the failing artifact, then request canary promote.
Priyanka: PR #3245 incoming with tests and CI eval. Will add a HOTFIX release note for customers who've pulled the broken conversion in the last 48h.
Maya: Great — if anyone else sees similar garbling on different imports please drop a short thread here.
